title: Swift, Erie, and federal general common law
shortTitle: Swift, Erie, and federal general common law
summary: Before Erie, Swift permitted federal courts to exercise independent judgment on some questions categorized as general law. Erie rejected that approach to state-law rights and required respect for state judicial decisions as well as statutes.
notes: Erie rejects federal general common law, while the course separately studies specialized federal common law justified by particular federal interests. Those are different claims of authority.

sections.Meaning: Before Erie, Swift permitted federal courts to exercise independent judgment on some questions categorized as general law. Erie rejected that approach to state-law rights and required respect for state judicial decisions as well as statutes.
sections.How to work through the question: Trace the asserted source of law in Swift, the strategic reincorporation in Black & White Taxicab, and the disputed railroad duty in Erie. Explain how federal forum choice affected the governing substantive standard.
